title: Python Async Testing And Production Questionnaire

questions.prompt: A Python async function is called but not awaited or scheduled. What is the senior review note?

options.label: It started immediately like most promise-returning JavaScript functions.
It created a coroutine object that will not run until awaited or scheduled.
It automatically moved to a background thread.

questions.explanation: Calling an async def returns a coroutine object. Execution requires awaiting it or scheduling it as a task.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap with the runtime resource blocked by sync work inside async Python code.
questions.template: A synchronous blocking call inside an async handler can stall the {{blank}}.
questions.explanation: Async syntax does not make blocking I/O or CPU-heavy work safe for the event loop.

questions.prompt: Order a safer background task ownership flow.

items.label: Retain a reference or group owner

questions.explanation: Background work needs lifetime ownership, error visibility, and cleanup.

questions.prompt: Match the asyncio concept to the production review lens.

pairs.match: awaitable work that has not necessarily been scheduled
scheduled coroutine with lifecycle ownership needs
explicit failure boundary for slow work

questions.explanation: The important distinction is not syntax; it is ownership, scheduling, and failure behavior.

questions.prompt: A flaky async test uses arbitrary sleeps to wait for work. What should a senior reviewer prefer?

options.label: Increase the sleep duration until the test passes locally.
Await observable state or test pure logic below the async wrapper.
Skip async behavior because it is hard to test.

questions.explanation: Reliable async tests wait on meaningful state or isolate pure behavior instead of depending on timers.

questions.prompt: Order the senior questions for choosing an async concurrency primitive.

items.label: Define what happens when one child operation fails
Define whether partial results are acceptable

questions.explanation: Concurrency primitives should be selected from the failure contract, not from surface syntax.

questions.prompt: When is asyncio.TaskGroup a strong fit in senior Python async code?

options.label: When child tasks share a scope and sibling cancellation should be explicit.
When background work should be forgotten after it is scheduled.
When CPU-heavy work needs to run faster on the event loop.

questions.explanation: TaskGroup expresses structured concurrency: child tasks belong to a scope and failures are handled as part of that scope.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap for what a timeout should represent in production async code.
questions.template: A timeout should be a domain-owned {{blank}}, not a magic number copied across adapters.
questions.explanation: Timeouts define when work becomes unavailable for the user or caller. They should be owned by the operation contract.

questions.prompt: Order the review flow for a long-lived async client or connection pool.

items.label: Create it at the application-owned boundary
Pass it to handlers or services explicitly
Log and trace operations through the adapter
Close it during shutdown or scope exit

questions.explanation: Resource lifetime should be visible and deterministic instead of controlled by import-time globals.

questions.prompt: Match each async production concept to the senior review concern.

pairs.match: resource state can leak between tests

questions.explanation: Senior production Python review connects async behavior, test stability, and observability to explicit ownership.
